risks: Shared CRM contracts/commands/repository are normative new files for multiple packages; creating independent versions before WP-24 receipts causes conflicting writers and lost integration.
Current local dos-* cards and name-matched touches are not canonical Company/Contact refs or authorization. Parser drops unknown fields, so an injected ref without parser update is lost after reload.

Company wrapper uses plain string+explicit mentions while generic parent contract uses RichText+attachments and no explicit mentions field; dropping mention payload or Contact support would silently narrow acceptance.

Current platform enum and canonical-result triad differ from broad operation schema; root must supply accepted common-kind and command result mapping, not invent WP-25-only aliases/status conventions.
Current Conation mutations are intentionally blocked. WP-25 must not use authPresent:true or fake schema evidence to enable outbound CRM write as a substitute for native shared discussion.
Mention is not sharing: stale index/snippet, push excerpt, attachment URL, hidden count and cached agent brief can leak private mail even if parent Company is shared.
WP-38/WP-26 consume WP-25; treating them as blocking direct predecessors creates a cycle. Agree interfaces while implementing required WP-25 privacy/context itself.
Claimed inbox lease must not equal processed effect; restart and replay must atomically preserve dedup and canonical command receipt.
Edit/delete must fence stale projection events and coalesce recipient attention; processing every event as a new notification yields an amplification bug.
Thread resolve/reaction/deleted-root policy, attachment denial and Contact discussion indexing appear in published CRM-DISCUSS-01 beyond the short seven criteria and cannot be omitted.
No runtime evidence exists in this preflight. Source hashes cover inspected working-tree bytes only; concurrent root integration invalidates affected references and demands reinspection.
Locale and common transport/tool registration implementations lie outside scoped inspected code; patch/interface requests are proposals from normative contracts, not verified existing exports.
